limitations: This is a separate, narrower objective than the draft service-failure-first protocol.
A packet preference is not evidence of better connectivity, radio outage or end-to-end loss.
Labels reflect realized paired outcomes, not an expectation over channel/RNG conditions.
Repeated/conflicting inputs must remain together; no random row split.
No independent validation/test evidence is currently available.
Primary training rows require source SHA256 verification; other audited labels are supplemental.
config_id hashes the exported partial configuration, not a complete resolved simulator configuration.
This dataset cannot establish RF generalization or improvement over A3.
The existing service-failure-first validated trainer is unchanged and is not compatible with this narrower protocol.
One scenario family and a single STAY example cannot support a defensible two-class train/validation split.
This prototype is fit on all eligible primary rows; no held-out accuracy is available.
A single STAY observation and four distinct inputs cannot establish a useful policy.
Training class weighting changes scores; 0.6 is the agreed initial threshold, not a calibrated confidence.
This export does not implement or validate an ns-3 policy and does not establish RF improvement over A3.
